243	**Section 4.7 --- \"Interrelated Wrongful Acts\"**
244	
245	\"Interrelated Wrongful Acts\" means Wrongful Acts that are the same, related, or arising from a common nucleus of facts, circumstances, situations, transactions, events, or series of related facts, circumstances, situations, transactions, or events, regardless of whether such Wrongful Acts involve the same or different Insured Persons, the same or different claimants, or the same or different legal theories.
246	
247	All Claims arising from Interrelated Wrongful Acts shall be deemed a single Claim for all purposes under this Policy, including the application of retentions and Limits of Liability. Such single Claim shall be deemed first made on the date the earliest of such Claims was first made, or on the date a Claim arising from the same Interrelated Wrongful Acts is first reported to the Insurer in writing, whichever is earlier. If any Claim arising from Interrelated Wrongful Acts was first made prior to the inception of the Policy Period, all Claims arising from such Interrelated Wrongful Acts shall be deemed first made prior to the Policy Period and shall not be covered under this Policy.
248	
249	**[ARTICLE III --- EXCLUSIONS]{.underline}**
250	
251	The Insurer shall not be liable to make any payment of Loss in connection with any Claim made against any Insured Person or the Company as set forth below:
252	
253	**Section 5.1 --- Conduct Exclusion**
254	
255	The Insurer shall not be liable for Loss arising from or attributable to any Claim based upon, arising out of, relating to, or in any way involving:
256	
257	> \(a\) any deliberate dishonest or fraudulent act or omission by an Insured Person, including but not limited to any act of fraud, embezzlement, or misappropriation;
258	>
259	> \(b\) any willful violation of any statute, rule, regulation, or law by an Insured Person, where such violation was committed with knowledge that the conduct in question constituted a violation; or
260	>
261	> \(c\) the gaining of any personal profit, remuneration, financial advantage, or other benefit to which such Insured Person was not legally entitled, including but not limited to any profit gained from the purchase or sale of securities in violation of Section 16(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 or any similar provision of state or foreign law.
262	
263	**Notwithstanding the foregoing, the exclusions set forth in clauses (a), (b), and (c) of this Section 5.1 shall apply only if and to the extent that such deliberate dishonesty, fraud, willful violation, or illegal personal profit or advantage is established by a final, non-appealable adjudication in the underlying action or proceeding giving rise to the Claim, or in a separate action or proceeding in a court of competent jurisdiction.** No allegation, accusation, stipulation, or admission (including but not limited to any admission in a plea agreement, consent order, or settlement) shall trigger this exclusion absent such final, non-appealable adjudication.
264	
265	The Insurer shall advance Defense Costs prior to any such final, non-appealable adjudication, in accordance with Section 9 of this Policy, subject to the Insured Person\'s agreement and undertaking to repay such Defense Costs to the Insurer if it is ultimately established by such final, non-appealable adjudication that the conduct described in clauses (a), (b), or (c) above has occurred with respect to such Insured Person.
266	
267	**Section 5.2 --- Insured vs. Insured Exclusion**
268	
269	The Insurer shall not be liable for Loss in connection with any Claim made against an Insured Person:
270

**[ARTICLE IV --- CONDITIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 6 --- Reporting Requirements**

**6.1 Notice of Claims.** The Named Insured or any Insured Person shall give written notice of any Claim to the Insurer at the address set forth in Item 10 of the Declarations as soon as practicable during the Policy Period or any applicable Discovery Period, but in no event later than sixty (60) days after the expiration of the Policy Period or any applicable Discovery Period, whichever is later.

**6.2 Contents of Notice.** Such notice shall include a description of the Claim, the identity of the claimant(s) and the Insured Person(s) against whom the Claim has been made, the date and manner in which the Claim was first made, the nature and circumstances of the Wrongful Act(s) alleged, the nature of the Loss claimed, and copies of all relevant pleadings, demands, subpoenas, and other documents.

**6.3 Notice-Prejudice Savings Clause.** The failure to give timely notice of a Claim in accordance with this Section 6 shall not bar or otherwise preclude coverage under this Policy unless the Insurer demonstrates that it has been actually and materially prejudiced by such failure. The burden of establishing actual and material prejudice shall rest with the Insurer. Late notice that does not actually and materially prejudice the Insurer shall not constitute a defense to coverage or a basis for denial or reduction of any covered Loss.

**6.4 Notice of Circumstances.** If, during the Policy Period, the Named Insured or any Insured Person becomes aware of specific circumstances that may reasonably be expected to give rise to a Claim, and gives written notice of such circumstances to the Insurer, including a description of the circumstances, the identities of the potential claimant(s) and the Insured Person(s) potentially involved, the reasons why such circumstances may reasonably be expected to give rise to a Claim, and the nature of the potential Wrongful Act, then any subsequent Claim arising from such noticed circumstances shall be deemed first made on the date such notice of circumstances was first received by the Insurer. Such notice shall be given during the Policy Period and shall be directed to the Insurer at the address set forth in Item 10 of the Declarations.

**Section 7 --- Defense and Settlement**

**7.1 No Duty to Defend.** The Insurer does not assume any duty to defend any Claim under this Policy. The Insured Persons and/or the Company shall have the right and the obligation to defend, investigate, and contest any Claim. The selection of defense counsel by the Insured Persons or the Company shall be subject to the prior written consent of the Insurer, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, or conditioned. The Insurer shall be entitled to effectively associate in the defense and the negotiation of any settlement of any Claim that involves or appears reasonably likely to involve the Insurer, including but not limited to the right to attend meetings with defense counsel, review and comment on significant pleadings and filings, participate in mediation and settlement discussions, and obtain copies of all material correspondence and court filings.

**7.2 Settlement Consent.** The Insurer shall not be liable for any settlement of any Claim unless such settlement is effected with the prior written consent of the Insurer. The Insurer\'s consent to any settlement shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, or conditioned, provided that the Insurer may withhold consent to any settlement that:

> \(a\) does not include a complete and unconditional release of all Insured Persons from all claims asserted by the claimant(s) in connection with such Claim;
>
> \(b\) imposes any non-monetary obligations, injunctive relief, or behavioral restrictions on any Insured Person;
>
> \(c\) involves an admission of wrongdoing, fault, or liability by any Insured Person; or
>
> \(d\) is funded in whole or in part from assets or resources not constituting covered Loss under this Policy.

**7.3 Hammer Clause.** If the Insurer recommends a settlement of a Claim within the applicable Limits of Liability and the Named Insured or the Insured Person refuses to consent to such settlement, the Insurer\'s liability for such Claim shall not exceed the sum of: (i) the amount for which the Insurer could have settled the Claim at the time the settlement was recommended, plus (ii) Defense Costs incurred up to and including the date of such settlement recommendation. Any additional Loss incurred after the date of the Insurer\'s settlement recommendation, including additional Defense Costs, excess judgments, and any settlement amount in excess of the Insurer\'s recommended settlement, shall be borne solely by the Named Insured or the Insured Person, as applicable.

**7.4 Cooperation.** The Company and all Insured Persons shall cooperate with the Insurer in the investigation, defense, and settlement of any Claim, and shall not admit liability, make any payment, assume any obligation, incur any expense (other than Defense Costs subject to advancement under Section 9), or consent to any judgment without the prior written consent of the Insurer. Any such admission, payment, assumption of obligation, or consent made without the Insurer\'s prior written consent shall not be binding upon the Insurer and shall not create any obligation on the part of the Insurer to pay any Loss arising therefrom.

**Section 8 --- Allocation**

**8.1** If a Claim against an Insured Person or the Company includes both covered and non-covered matters, both covered and non-covered parties, or both covered and non-covered Loss, or if a Claim is made against both Insured Persons who are covered under this Policy and other individuals or entities who are not covered under this Policy, the Insurer and the Named Insured shall use their best efforts to agree upon a fair and proper allocation of covered Loss, taking into account the relative legal and financial exposure of the parties, the nature of the covered and non-covered allegations, and all other relevant considerations.

**8.2** If the Insurer and the Named Insured cannot agree on the appropriate allocation, the allocation shall be determined by reference to the relative legal and financial exposure attributable to the covered versus non-covered matters, parties, and Loss, as determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or by binding arbitration in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association.

**8.3** Pending agreement on the appropriate allocation, or pending a determination by a court or arbitration panel, the Insurer shall advance seventy percent (70%) of Defense Costs on a current basis, subject to a final true-up and adjustment upon agreement or final determination of the proper allocation. Any overpayment by the Insurer shall be repaid promptly by the Named Insured or the Insured Persons, as applicable, and any underpayment by the Insurer shall be paid promptly by the Insurer.

**Section 9 --- Advancement of Defense Costs**

**9.1** The Insurer acknowledges the critical importance of the timely advancement of Defense Costs to Insured Persons. The Insurer agrees that Defense Costs covered under this Policy shall be advanced on a current basis, prior to the final disposition of a Claim, to the extent that such Defense Costs are covered under the applicable Insuring Clause and are not subject to an exclusion under this Policy that has been established by a final, non-appealable adjudication.

**9.2** The Insured Person or the Company (on behalf of an Insured Person) shall submit invoices for Defense Costs to the Insurer at the address set forth in Item 10 of the Declarations, together with reasonable supporting documentation establishing that such costs were incurred in connection with the investigation, defense, or appeal of a covered Claim. Such documentation shall include, at a minimum, copies of invoices from defense counsel or other service providers, a general description of the services rendered (provided that the Insurer shall not require the disclosure of privileged communications or attorney work product), and the applicable Claim reference number.

**9.3** The Insurer shall advance Defense Costs within **sixty (60) days** of receipt of invoices and supporting documentation that reasonably establish that such costs constitute covered Defense Costs under this Policy. If the Insurer disputes that any portion of the invoiced Defense Costs constitutes covered Defense Costs, the Insurer shall so notify the Insured Person or the Company in writing within such sixty (60) day period, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute. The Insurer shall advance the undisputed portion of Defense Costs within the sixty (60) day period, and the disputed portion shall be resolved in accordance with Section 8 (Allocation) or Section 20 (Governing Law) of this Policy, as applicable.

**9.4** If it is subsequently determined by a final, non-appealable adjudication that a Claim is not covered under this Policy, or that the Conduct Exclusion set forth in Section 5.1 applies to a particular Insured Person, such Insured Person(s) shall repay to the Insurer any Defense Costs previously advanced by the Insurer with respect to such Claim or such Insured Person. The Named Insured shall use its best efforts to cause any Insured Person to execute an undertaking to repay advanced Defense Costs upon the Insurer\'s reasonable request.

**9.5** The Insurer\'s obligation to advance Defense Costs under this Section 9 shall apply regardless of whether the Insured Person has been indemnified by the Company, and regardless of whether the Company has submitted or intends to submit a claim for reimbursement under Insuring Clause B. The Insurer\'s obligation to advance Defense Costs is independent of and not contingent upon the Company\'s indemnification obligations to the Insured Person.

**Section 10 --- Discovery Period (Extended Reporting Period)**

**10.1 Availability.** If this Policy is not renewed by the Insurer, or if this Policy is cancelled by the Insurer for any reason other than non-payment of premium, the Named Insured shall have the right to purchase a Discovery Period by providing written notice to the Insurer and paying the applicable additional premium set forth in Item 7 of the Declarations. Such written notice and payment must be received by the Insurer within **thirty (30) days** after the end of the Policy Period (i.e., no later than January 31, 2026, for the current Policy Period ending January 1, 2026). The right to purchase a Discovery Period is exercisable only by the Named Insured and is not transferable or assignable.

**10.2 Discovery Period Options.** The Named Insured may elect one of the following Discovery Period options:

> \(a\) **12-Month Discovery Period:** A Discovery Period of twelve (12) months following the expiration of the Policy Period, for an additional premium equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the annual premium, which is \$1,340,000.
>
> \(b\) **24-Month Discovery Period:** A Discovery Period of twenty-four (24) months following the expiration of the Policy Period, for an additional premium equal to one hundred seventy-five percent (175%) of the annual premium, which is \$2,345,000.

**10.3 Scope of Discovery Period.** The Discovery Period shall extend the period during which Claims may be first made against an Insured Person or the Company and reported to the Insurer, but only with respect to Wrongful Acts that occurred prior to the end of the Policy Period. No Wrongful Act first committed or occurring during the Discovery Period shall be covered under this Policy. The Discovery Period is an extension of the reporting period only and does not extend the period during which covered Wrongful Acts may occur.

**10.4 Limitations on Discovery Period.** The Discovery Period shall not be available if:

> \(a\) the Named Insured has obtained any replacement directors and officers liability insurance policy, or any insurance policy that is substantially similar in coverage to this Policy, from any insurer (including the Insurer), regardless of whether such replacement policy provides the same or different terms, conditions, limits, or retentions;
>
> \(b\) this Policy has been cancelled for non-payment of premium;
>
> \(c\) the Named Insured fails to provide written notice and pay the applicable Discovery Period premium within the thirty (30) day period specified in Section 10.1 above; or
>
> \(d\) this Policy was cancelled at the request of the Named Insured.

**10.5 Limits During Discovery Period.** The aggregate Limits of Liability applicable during the Discovery Period shall be part of and not in addition to the aggregate Limits of Liability for the Policy Period as set forth in Item 4 of the Declarations. The Discovery Period does not provide any additional aggregate limit of liability beyond the limits available during the Policy Period. Any Loss paid during the Policy Period shall reduce the Limits of Liability available during the Discovery Period, and any Loss paid during the Discovery Period shall reduce the remaining Limits of Liability. The total combined liability of the Insurer during the Policy Period and any Discovery Period shall not exceed the aggregate Limits of Liability set forth in Item 4 of the Declarations.

**Section 11 --- Severability**

**11.1 Severability of Conduct Exclusion.** With respect to the Conduct Exclusion set forth in Section 5.1 of this Policy, no Wrongful Act of one Insured Person shall be imputed to any other Insured Person for the purpose of determining the applicability of such exclusion. The knowledge, intent, acts, errors, omissions, or statements of one Insured Person shall not be imputed to any other Insured Person. Each Insured Person\'s coverage under this Policy shall be determined independently and without reference to the conduct of any other Insured Person.

**11.2 Severability of Application.** The Application for this Policy is deemed severed as between each Insured Person. Solely with respect to any determination as to whether the Application contains any material misrepresentation, inaccuracy, or nondisclosure:

> \(a\) the statements, representations, and warranties contained in the Application and any supplemental application materials shall be deemed to be the statements, representations, and warranties of the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer of the Named Insured only, and not the statements, representations, or warranties of any other Insured Person;
>
> \(b\) no coverage under this Policy shall be rescinded, voided, or otherwise affected as to any Insured Person other than the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer of the Named Insured, unless such other Insured Person had actual knowledge, as opposed to imputed, constructive, or should-have-known knowledge, of the alleged misrepresentation, inaccuracy, or nondisclosure at the time the Application was submitted to the Insurer;
>
> \(c\) the Insurer\'s remedies with respect to any misrepresentation, inaccuracy, or nondisclosure in the Application shall be limited to rescission or modification of coverage solely with respect to those Insured Persons described in clauses (a) and (b) above, and shall not affect the coverage of any other Insured Person.

The provisions of this Section 11 shall apply to all Insuring Clauses and all endorsements attached to this Policy.

**Section 12 --- Subrogation**

**12.1 General Subrogation.** Upon and to the extent of payment of any Loss under this Policy, the Insurer shall be subrogated to all of the Insured Person\'s or the Company\'s rights of recovery against any person or entity (other than an Insured Person, to the extent provided in Section 12.2 below). The Insurer\'s subrogation rights shall include, without limitation, all rights of recovery, contribution, and indemnification against any third party that may be liable for any portion of the Loss paid by the Insurer.

**Section 13 --- Other Insurance**

**13.1** Except as otherwise provided herein, this Policy shall be excess over any other valid and collectible insurance (whether primary, excess, contingent, or otherwise) available to the Company or any Insured Person, including but not limited to any policy maintained by an Outside Entity on behalf of an Insured Person. **13.2** Notwithstanding Section 13.1, with respect to Insuring Clause A (Side A --- Non-Indemnifiable Loss), this Policy shall be primary and non-contributory with respect to any other insurance available to an Insured Person (other than any personal directors and officers liability policy maintained by the Insured Person at the Insured Person\'s own expense), and the Insurer shall not seek contribution from any such other insurance. Coverage under Insuring Clause A shall respond without regard to the existence or availability of any other insurance, except as specifically stated in this Section 13.2.

**Section 14 --- Order of Payments**

**14.1** In the event that the aggregate Limits of Liability under this Policy are insufficient to pay all covered Loss arising from all Claims during the Policy Period and any applicable Discovery Period, the Insurer shall prioritize payments as follows:

> \(a\) **First**, the Insurer shall pay all covered Loss under Insuring Clause A (Side A --- Non-Indemnifiable Loss), up to the applicable dedicated aggregate limit of \$25,000,000;
>
> \(b\) **Second**, the Insurer shall pay all covered Loss under Insuring Clause B (Side B --- Corporate Reimbursement), up to the remaining applicable combined aggregate limit shared with Insuring Clause C;
>
> \(c\) **Third**, the Insurer shall pay all covered Loss under Insuring Clause C (Side C --- Entity Securities Coverage), up to the remaining applicable combined aggregate limit shared with Insuring Clause B.

**14.2** No payment of Loss under Insuring Clause B or Insuring Clause C shall be made if and to the extent that such payment would reduce the Limits of Liability available to pay Loss under Insuring Clause A. The Insurer and the Named Insured acknowledge and agree that the protection of individual directors and officers through Insuring Clause A is a priority objective of this Policy.

**Section 15 --- Territory**

This Policy shall apply to Claims first made and Wrongful Acts committed anywhere in the world, subject to all of the terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of this Policy. The Insurer shall have no obligation to pay any Loss in any currency other than United States dollars, and all payments shall be made in United States dollars at the applicable exchange rate on the date of payment.

**Section 16 --- Cancellation and Non-Renewal**

**16.1 Cancellation by Insurer.** The Insurer may cancel this Policy only for non-payment of premium. In the event of cancellation for non-payment, the Insurer shall provide thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of cancellation to the Named Insured at the address set forth in Item 1 of the Declarations. If the Named Insured pays all outstanding premium within such thirty (30) day period, the cancellation shall be rescinded and the Policy shall remain in full force and effect.

**16.2 Non-Renewal by Insurer.** The Insurer shall provide not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice of non-renewal to the Named Insured at the address set forth in Item 1 of the Declarations.

**16.3 Cancellation by Named Insured.** The Named Insured may cancel this Policy at any time by written notice to the Insurer at the address set forth in Item 9 of the Declarations. In the event of cancellation by the Named Insured, the return premium shall be computed on a short-rate basis in accordance with the Insurer\'s standard short-rate cancellation table.

**16.4 Discovery Period upon Cancellation or Non-Renewal.** Upon cancellation by the Insurer (other than for non-payment of premium) or non-renewal by the Insurer, the Named Insured\'s right to purchase a Discovery Period pursuant to Section 10 of this Policy shall apply.

**Section 17 --- Representations and Warranty**

The Named Insured represents and warrants that the statements, representations, and information contained in the Application and all supplemental materials submitted to the Insurer are true, accurate, and complete as of the date of the Application. The Application is incorporated into and forms a part of this Policy. The Named Insured acknowledges that the Insurer has issued this Policy in reliance upon the truth, accuracy, and completeness of such statements, representations, and information. The provisions of Section 11 (Severability) shall apply to any determination as to the effect of any misrepresentation, inaccuracy, or nondisclosure in the Application.

**Section 18 --- Entire Agreement / Amendments**

This Policy, together with the Application, the Declarations, and any endorsements attached hereto and forming a part hereof, constitutes the entire agreement between the Insurer and the Named Insured with respect to the subject matter hereof. No other agreement, representation, promise, or understanding, whether written or oral, shall modify or affect this Policy. No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Policy shall be effective unless set forth in a written endorsement issued by the Insurer and attached to this Policy.

**Section 19 --- Authorization**

The Named Insured shall act on behalf of all Insured Persons for all purposes under this Policy, including but not limited to giving and receiving notice, paying premiums, receiving return premiums, making elections (including the election to purchase a Discovery Period), requesting endorsements, and communicating with the Insurer and the Insurance Broker. Except with respect to coverage under Insuring Clause A (Side A --- Non-Indemnifiable Loss), the Named Insured shall act on behalf of all Insured Persons with respect to all matters relating to this Policy, and the Insurer shall be entitled to rely upon the acts and representations of the Named Insured as binding upon all Insured Persons.

**Section 20 --- Governing Law**

This Policy shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles. Any dispute arising under or relating to this Policy shall be resolved in accordance with Delaware law, and the parties consent to the jurisdiction of the courts of the State of Delaware for the resolution of any such dispute.

> \(c\) **Refusal to Indemnify.** The Company refuses to indemnify the Insured Person in breach of its obligations under applicable law, its certificate of incorporation, bylaws, or any indemnification agreement between the Company and the Insured Person, and such refusal results in the Insured Person bearing Loss that would otherwise have been covered by indemnification.

For the avoidance of doubt, if the Company has entered into an indemnification agreement with an Insured Person obligating the Company to indemnify such Insured Person for specified losses, expenses, or liabilities, and the Company fails, refuses, or is unable to fulfill such obligation in whole or in part, such Loss shall constitute Non-Indemnifiable Loss under Insuring Clause A to the extent of the Company\'s failure, refusal, or inability to indemnify.

This Endorsement does not create any additional Limits of Liability beyond those set forth in Item 4 of the Declarations. The dedicated Side A aggregate limit of \$25,000,000 shall apply to all Loss payable under Insuring Clause A, whether arising under this Endorsement or otherwise.

All other terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of the Policy remain unchanged and in full force and effect.

**[Endorsement No. 3 --- Order of Payments Endorsement]{.underline}**

**Endorsement No.: RSI-DO-END-003 Effective Date: January 1, 2025 Attached to and Forming Part of Policy No. RSI-DO-2025-07741 Issued to: Ferndale BioSciences, Inc.**

This Endorsement restates and reinforces the Order of Payments provision set forth in Section 14 of the Policy. In consideration of the premium charged, it is hereby understood and agreed as follows:

**Priority of Payments.** In the event that the aggregate Limits of Liability under this Policy are insufficient to pay all covered Loss arising from all Claims during the Policy Period and any applicable Discovery Period, the Insurer shall prioritize payments in the following order:

> \(1\) **First Priority**: All Loss payable under Insuring Clause A (Side A --- Non-Indemnifiable Loss);
>
> \(2\) **Second Priority**: All Loss payable under Insuring Clause B (Side B --- Corporate Reimbursement);
>
> \(3\) **Third Priority**: All Loss payable under Insuring Clause C (Side C --- Entity Securities Coverage).

**Protection of Side A Limits.** No payment of Loss under Insuring Clause B or Insuring Clause C shall be made that would reduce, erode, or exhaust the Limits of Liability available to pay Loss under Insuring Clause A. The Named Insured and the Insurer acknowledge and agree that the Side A dedicated limit of \$25,000,000 as set forth in Item 4 of the Declarations is not shared with and is not eroded by payments under Insuring Clause B or Insuring Clause C. The Insurer shall not apply or allocate any payment under Insuring Clause B or Insuring Clause C against the Side A dedicated limit.

**Application to All Claims.** The priority of payments set forth in this Endorsement shall apply to all Claims, whether arising from the same or different Wrongful Acts, whether involving the same or different Insured Persons, and whether made during the Policy Period or any applicable Discovery Period. In the event of simultaneous or overlapping Claims implicating multiple Insuring Clauses, the Insurer shall honor the priority structure established herein.

All other terms, conditions, exclusions, and limitations of the Policy remain unchanged and in full force and effect.

**FENWICK BIOSCIENCES, INC.**

**INDEMNIFICATION AGREEMENT**

This Indemnification Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of \[**\_\_**\], 2025 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between Fenwick BioSciences, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the \"Company\"), and \[**\_\_**\] (the \"Indemnitee\").

The Company is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its shares of common stock listed and traded on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the ticker symbol \"FWKB,\" and maintains its principal executive offices at 400 Concord Avenue, Suite 800, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138.

**WHEREAS**, the Company recognizes that competent and experienced persons are increasingly reluctant to serve as directors and officers of public corporations unless they are provided with adequate protection through indemnification and insurance against the risks of claims and actions arising out of their service to and activities on behalf of the corporation, and that the exposure to litigation costs and legal fees arising out of such service may be so significant as to deter highly qualified individuals from accepting these positions;

**WHEREAS**, the Board of Directors of the Company (the \"Board\") has determined that the inability to attract and retain such qualified persons as directors and officers of the Company would be detrimental to the best interests of the Company and its stockholders, and that the Company should act to assure such persons that there will be increased certainty of such protection in the future;

**WHEREAS**, the Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Chapter 1 of the Delaware Code (the \"DGCL\"), specifically Section 145 thereof, empowers Delaware corporations to indemnify their directors, officers, employees, and agents in connection with actions, suits, and proceedings, and Section 102(b)(7) of the DGCL permits a corporation to include in its certificate of incorporation a provision eliminating or limiting the personal liability of a director to the corporation or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director, subject to certain exceptions;

**WHEREAS**, the Company\'s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the \"Certificate of Incorporation\") and Amended and Restated Bylaws (the \"Bylaws\") provide for the indemnification of the directors and officers of the Company to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL, and this Agreement is intended to supplement and further the indemnification provisions of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Bylaws, and any resolutions adopted by the Board pursuant thereto, and shall not be deemed a substitute therefor, nor to diminish or abrogate any rights of the Indemnitee thereunder;

**WHEREAS**, the Indemnitee is willing to serve, continue to serve, or provide additional service for or on behalf of the Company on the condition that the Indemnitee be so indemnified and that the Indemnitee\'s rights to indemnification and advancement of expenses be set forth in a separate written agreement between the Indemnitee and the Company; and

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the Indemnitee\'s agreement to serve or continue to serve the Company in the Indemnitee\'s current capacity and in such other capacities as the Indemnitee may hereafter be asked to serve, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows:

**[Section 1. Definitions]{.underline}**

For purposes of this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

> **(a)** \"Board\" means the Board of Directors of the Company.
>
> **(b)** \"Change of Control\" means the occurrence of any of the following events after the Effective Date: (i) the acquisition by any person, entity, or \"group\" (within the meaning of Section 13(d)(3) or 14(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the \"Exchange Act\")) of beneficial ownership (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 promulgated under the Exchange Act) of securities of the Company representing fifty percent (50%) or more of the combined voting power of the Company\'s then-outstanding voting securities entitled to vote generally in the election of directors; (ii) the consummation of a merger, consolidation, reorganization, recapitalization, or similar corporate transaction involving the Company (a \"Business Combination\"), unless, following such Business Combination, the stockholders of the Company immediately prior thereto continue to beneficially own, directly or indirectly, at least fifty percent (50%) of the combined voting power of the then-outstanding voting securities entitled to vote generally in the election of directors of the entity resulting from such Business Combination (including, without limitation, an entity that, as a result of such transaction, owns the Company or all or substantially all of the Company\'s assets either directly or through one or more subsidiaries) in substantially the same proportions as their ownership of the Company\'s voting securities immediately prior to such Business Combination; (iii) the sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company; or (iv) a change in the composition of the Board such that the individuals who, as of the Effective Date, constitute the Board (such Board being hereinafter referred to as the \"Incumbent Board\") cease for any reason to constitute at least a majority of the Board over any period of twenty-four (24) consecutive months; *provided, however*, that any individual becoming a director subsequent to the Effective Date whose election, or nomination for election by the Company\'s stockholders, was approved by a vote of at least a majority of the directors then comprising the Incumbent Board shall be considered as though such individual were a member of the Incumbent Board, but excluding, for this purpose, any such individual whose initial assumption of office occurs as a result of an actual or threatened election contest with respect to the election or removal of directors or other actual or threatened solicitation of proxies or consents by or on behalf of a person other than the Board.
>
> **(c)** \"Corporate Status\" means the status of a person as a current or former director, officer, employee, or agent of the Company, or as a current or former director, officer, employee, agent, trustee, or fiduciary of any other Enterprise serving at the request of the Company. For the avoidance of doubt, service as a director, officer, employee, agent, trustee, or fiduciary of an Enterprise shall be deemed to be at the request of the Company if the Indemnitee serves or served in such capacity as a result of the Company\'s direct or indirect ownership interest in the Enterprise or the Company\'s appointment, nomination, election, or designation of the Indemnitee to serve in such capacity.
>
> **(d)** \"Disinterested Director\" means a director of the Company who is not and was not a party to the Proceeding in respect of which indemnification is sought by the Indemnitee pursuant to this Agreement.
>
> **(e)** \"Enterprise\" means any corporation, partnership, joint venture, limited liability company, trust, employee benefit plan, or other entity or enterprise for which the Indemnitee serves or has served as a director, officer, employee, agent, trustee, or fiduciary at the request of the Company. For purposes of this Agreement, service to an employee benefit plan shall include any service that imposes duties on, or involves services by, the Indemnitee with respect to an employee benefit plan, its participants, or its beneficiaries, including acting as a fiduciary thereof.
>
> **(f)** \"Expenses\" means all reasonable and actually incurred attorneys\' fees, retainers, court costs, transcript costs, fees of experts and other professionals, witness fees, travel expenses, duplicating costs, printing and binding costs, telephone charges, postage, delivery service fees, any Federal, state, local, or foreign taxes imposed on the Indemnitee as a result of the actual or deemed receipt of any payments under this Agreement, Freedom of Information Act or other public records access request fees, and all other disbursements, costs, or expenses of the types customarily incurred in connection with prosecuting, defending, preparing to prosecute or defend, investigating, being or preparing to be a witness in, settling, or otherwise participating in a Proceeding, including, without limitation, the costs of complying with any court order, consent decree, judgment, or other directive arising from or in connection with a Proceeding. Expenses shall also include Expenses incurred in connection with any appeal resulting from any Proceeding and any Expenses incurred in establishing a right to indemnification under this Agreement.
>
> **(g)** \"Fines\" means any fine, penalty, or excise tax assessed against the Indemnitee in connection with a Proceeding, including, without limitation, any excise tax assessed with respect to an employee benefit plan under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended, or any similar federal, state, or local statute or regulation.
>
> **(h)** \"Independent Counsel\" means a law firm, or a member of a law firm, that is experienced in matters of corporation law and neither presently is, nor in the past five (5) years has been, retained to represent: (i) the Company or the Indemnitee in any matter material to either such party (other than with respect to matters concerning the Indemnitee under this Agreement, or of other indemnitees under similar indemnification agreements); or (ii) any other party to the Proceeding giving rise to a claim for indemnification hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the term \"Independent Counsel\" shall not include any person who, under the applicable standards of professional conduct then prevailing, would have a conflict of interest in representing either the Company or the Indemnitee in an action to determine the Indemnitee\'s rights under this Agreement.
>
> **(i)** \"Proceeding\" means any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, arbitration, mediation, alternate dispute resolution mechanism, investigation (whether formal or informal), inquiry, hearing, or any other actual or threatened proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, regulatory, legislative, or investigative (including, without limitation, any investigation by a governmental authority or self-regulatory organization), including any appeal therefrom. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Proceeding\" includes a proceeding initiated by the Indemnitee to enforce the Indemnitee\'s rights under this Agreement, subject to the provisions of Section 7.
>
> **(j)** \"Amounts Paid in Settlement\" means any amounts paid in settlement of a Proceeding, including, without limitation, the value of any non-monetary consideration provided in connection with a settlement, as determined by the Board in its reasonable judgment.

**[Section 2. Indemnification --- Third-Party Proceedings]{.underline}**

The Company shall indemnify the Indemnitee, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, as such may be amended from time to time (but, in the case of any such amendment, only to the extent that such amendment permits the Company to provide broader indemnification rights than the applicable law permitted the Company to provide prior to such amendment). Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, if the Indemnitee was, is, or at any time becomes a party to or participant in, or is threatened to be made a party to or participant in, any Proceeding (other than a Proceeding by or in the right of the Company) by reason of (or arising in part out of) the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, the Company shall indemnify the Indemnitee against all Expenses, judgments, Fines, and Amounts Paid in Settlement actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee or on the Indemnitee\'s behalf in connection with such Proceeding or any claim, issue, or matter therein, to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL and other applicable law.

The indemnification provided under this Section 2 shall be contingent upon a determination, made in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 6 of this Agreement, that the Indemnitee acted in good faith and in a manner the Indemnitee reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company and, with respect to any criminal Proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe the Indemnitee\'s conduct was unlawful. The standard of conduct set forth in this Section 2 is consistent with the standard established by Section 145(a) of the DGCL.

The termination of any Proceeding by judgment, order, settlement, conviction, or upon a plea of nolo contendere or its equivalent, shall not, of itself, create a presumption that the Indemnitee did not act in good faith and in a manner which the Indemnitee reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company, and, with respect to any criminal Proceeding, shall not, of itself, create a presumption that the Indemnitee had reasonable cause to believe that the Indemnitee\'s conduct was unlawful. The Company acknowledges that the indemnification obligations under this Section 2 extend to all categories of loss specified herein, including, without limitation, Fines and penalties imposed by any governmental authority or regulatory body, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

**[Section 3. Indemnification --- Proceedings by or in the Right of the Company]{.underline}**

If the Indemnitee was, is, or at any time becomes a party to or participant in, or is threatened to be made a party to or participant in, any Proceeding by or in the right of the Company to procure a judgment in its favor by reason of (or arising in part out of) the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, the Company shall indemnify the Indemnitee against all Expenses actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee or on the Indemnitee\'s behalf in connection with such Proceeding or any claim, issue, or matter therein, to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL and other applicable law.

The indemnification provided under this Section 3 shall be contingent upon a determination, made in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 6 of this Agreement, that the Indemnitee acted in good faith and in a manner the Indemnitee reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company. The standard of conduct set forth in this Section 3 is consistent with the standard established by Section 145(b) of the DGCL.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, no indemnification for Expenses shall be made under this Section 3 in respect of any claim, issue, or matter as to which the Indemnitee shall have been adjudged to be liable to the Company, **unless** and only to the extent that the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, or the court in which such Proceeding was brought, shall determine upon application that, despite the adjudication of liability but in view of all the circumstances of the case, the Indemnitee is fairly and reasonably entitled to indemnification for such Expenses as such court shall deem proper. The parties acknowledge that this limitation reflects the mandatory restriction set forth in Section 145(b) of the DGCL.

For the avoidance of doubt, the scope of Proceedings covered by this Section 3 includes derivative actions brought by stockholders on behalf of the Company. Nothing in this Section 3 or elsewhere in this Agreement shall be construed to limit the Company\'s indemnification obligations under Section 2 with respect to any direct claim or Proceeding brought by the Company or any of its affiliates against the Indemnitee, which shall be governed by the provisions of Section 2.

**[Section 4. Indemnification for Expenses as a Witness or Participant]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding any limitation set forth in Sections 2 or 3 of this Agreement, to the extent that the Indemnitee is, by reason of the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, a witness in, or is called upon to respond to discovery requests, subpoenas, or other compulsory process in, or otherwise participates in, any Proceeding to which the Indemnitee is not a named party, the Company shall indemnify the Indemnitee against all Expenses actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee or on the Indemnitee\'s behalf in connection therewith. The indemnification provided under this Section 4 shall not be subject to the satisfaction of any standard of conduct and shall not require any determination of entitlement pursuant to the procedures set forth in Section 6. The Company\'s obligation under this Section 4 shall apply regardless of the nature of the Proceeding or the identity of the parties thereto.

**[Section 5. Advancement of Expenses]{.underline}**

The Company shall advance all Expenses incurred by the Indemnitee in connection with any Proceeding within thirty (30) days after receipt by the Company of a written request for such advancement from the Indemnitee, together with such documentation and information as is reasonably available to the Indemnitee and is reasonably necessary for the Company to determine whether the Indemnitee is entitled to advancement of Expenses hereunder. The Indemnitee\'s right to advancement of Expenses shall include, but not be limited to, the right to be advanced the Expenses of retaining counsel of the Indemnitee\'s choice. The Indemnitee\'s entitlement to advancement of Expenses under this Section 5 shall include Expenses incurred in connection with any Proceeding by or in the right of the Company, any third-party Proceeding, or any other Proceeding as described in this Agreement.

As a condition to the Company\'s obligation to advance Expenses pursuant to this Section 5, the Indemnitee hereby undertakes to repay all amounts so advanced if, and to the extent that, it shall ultimately be determined by final judicial decision from which there is no further right of appeal that the Indemnitee is not entitled to be indemnified by the Company under this Agreement or otherwise. The Indemnitee\'s obligation to repay such advances shall be unsecured, and no interest shall be charged thereon. No security shall be required by the Company in connection with any such undertaking.

The Company shall not impose any conditions on the advancement of Expenses beyond the undertaking described in the preceding paragraph. Specifically, and without limitation, the Company\'s obligation to advance Expenses shall not be subject to the satisfaction of any standard of conduct, and the Company shall advance Expenses without regard to whether the Indemnitee has met the standard of conduct set forth in Sections 2 or 3 of this Agreement. Any advances made pursuant to this Section 5 shall be made on a current basis, without regard to the Indemnitee\'s ability to repay such advances, and without regard to the Indemnitee\'s ultimate entitlement to indemnification under this Agreement or otherwise.

The right of the Indemnitee to advancement of Expenses pursuant to this Section 5 is a contractual right that shall be enforceable by the Indemnitee in any court of competent jurisdiction. The Company\'s obligation to advance Expenses is independent of its obligation to indemnify the Indemnitee and shall be enforceable independently thereof.

**[Section 6. Determination of Entitlement to Indemnification]{.underline}**

**(a) Mandatory Indemnification Upon Success.** To the extent that the Indemnitee has been successful on the merits or otherwise in the defense of any Proceeding referred to in Section 2 or Section 3 of this Agreement, or in defense of any claim, issue, or matter therein, the Company shall indemnify the Indemnitee against all Expenses actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee in connection therewith. For purposes of this Section 6(a), the termination of any such Proceeding or claim, issue, or matter therein by dismissal, with or without prejudice, shall be deemed to be a successful result, and the Indemnitee shall be deemed to have been successful on the merits or otherwise with respect to such terminated Proceeding, claim, issue, or matter. This provision reflects the mandatory indemnification requirement of Section 145(c) of the DGCL and shall be applied without any determination of entitlement pursuant to Section 6(b) below.

**(b) Determination Process.** In all cases not covered by Section 6(a), a determination shall be made that the Indemnitee has met the applicable standard of conduct set forth in Section 2 or Section 3, as applicable. Such determination shall be made as follows:

> \(i\) by a majority vote of the Disinterested Directors, even though less than a quorum of the Board;
>
> \(ii\) by a committee of Disinterested Directors designated by a majority vote of the Disinterested Directors, even though less than a quorum of the Board;
>
> \(iii\) if there are no Disinterested Directors, or if the Disinterested Directors so direct, by Independent Counsel in a written opinion to the Board, a copy of which shall be delivered to the Indemnitee; or
>
> \(iv\) by the stockholders of the Company.

The Board shall select the method of determination from among clauses (i) through (iv) above at its election; *provided, however*, that if a Change of Control shall have occurred and the Indemnitee so requests, the determination of entitlement to indemnification shall be made by Independent Counsel selected as provided in this Section 6(b)(iii), and not by the Board, a committee of the Board, or the stockholders. In the event that Independent Counsel is to make the determination, the Independent Counsel shall be selected by the Indemnitee and approved by the Company (which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). If the Company and the Indemnitee are unable to agree upon the selection of Independent Counsel within fifteen (15) days following the Company\'s receipt of the Indemnitee\'s request for indemnification, either the Company or the Indemnitee may petition the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware to appoint Independent Counsel. The Company shall pay the reasonable fees and expenses of any Independent Counsel engaged pursuant to this Section 6(b).

**(c) Deemed Approval.** If a determination of entitlement to indemnification under this Section 6 is required but has not been made within sixty (60) days after receipt by the Company of the Indemnitee\'s written request for indemnification (together with all documentation and information reasonably available to the Indemnitee and reasonably necessary for the Company to make such determination), the Indemnitee shall be deemed to have satisfied the applicable standard of conduct, and the Company\'s indemnification obligations under this Agreement shall be deemed approved and payable in full. The sixty (60)-day period set forth herein shall be tolled during any period in which the Company and the Indemnitee are negotiating in good faith regarding the selection of Independent Counsel pursuant to Section 6(b)(iii).

**[Section 7. Exclusions from Indemnification]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, the Company shall not be obligated under this Agreement to indemnify the Indemnitee in connection with:

> **(a) Proceedings Initiated by the Indemnitee.** Any Proceeding (or any part thereof) initiated or brought voluntarily by the Indemnitee against the Company or any director, officer, employee, or agent of the Company, unless (i) the Board of Directors authorized the Proceeding (or any part thereof) prior to its initiation, (ii) the Company provides the indemnification, in its sole discretion, pursuant to the powers vested in the Company under applicable law, or (iii) the Proceeding is brought by the Indemnitee to enforce the Indemnitee\'s rights under this Agreement as provided in Section 9 of this Agreement (in which case the provisions of Section 9 shall govern).
>
> **(b) Section 16(b) Disgorgement.** Any Proceeding or claim to the extent it requires the disgorgement of profits made from the purchase and sale (or sale and purchase) of securities of the Company within the meaning of Section 16(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or similar provisions of any applicable state statutory law or common law, it being understood that this exclusion applies solely to the amount of profits required to be disgorged and not to any Expenses incurred by the Indemnitee in connection with any such Proceeding.
>
> **(c) Clawback Obligations.** Any reimbursement or repayment of compensation paid to the Indemnitee that is required by (i) any clawback, recoupment, forfeiture, or similar policy adopted by the Company pursuant to the listing standards of any national securities exchange or association on which the Company\'s securities are listed, or pursuant to any other requirement of applicable law, including Rule 10D-1 promulgated under the Exchange Act, or (ii) Section 304 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 or Section 954 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, or any rules or regulations promulgated thereunder. For the avoidance of doubt, this exclusion applies solely to the amount of compensation required to be reimbursed or repaid and not to any Expenses incurred by the Indemnitee in connection with any proceeding or investigation relating to such clawback or recoupment.
>
> **(d) Settlements Without Consent.** Amounts Paid in Settlement of any Proceeding without the prior written consent of the Company, which consent shall not be un

The Company shall be deemed to have consented to a proposed settlement if the Company has not provided a written response to the Indemnitee\'s written request for consent within thirty (30) days after receipt of such request, together with a description of the material terms of the proposed settlement and all relevant documentation reasonably available to the Indemnitee.

The exclusions set forth in this Section 7 are intended to be the sole and exclusive exclusions from the Company\'s indemnification obligations under this Agreement. No exclusion, limitation, or condition not expressly set forth in this Section 7 shall be imposed on the Company\'s indemnification obligations hereunder, except as required by applicable law.

**[Section 8. Presumptions and Burden of Proof]{.underline}**

In making a determination with respect to the Indemnitee\'s entitlement to indemnification hereunder, the person, persons, or entity making such determination shall, to the fullest extent not prohibited by law, presume that the Indemnitee is entitled to indemnification under this Agreement. Anyone seeking to overcome this presumption shall have the burden of proof, and the Company shall have the burden of proof to overcome such presumption in the Company\'s favor by clear and convincing evidence. Neither the failure of the Company (including its Board, any committee thereof, Independent Counsel, or stockholders) to have made a determination prior to the commencement of any action pursuant to this Agreement that indemnification is proper in the circumstances because the Indemnitee has met the applicable standard of conduct, nor an actual determination by the Company (including its Board, any committee thereof, Independent Counsel, or stockholders) that the Indemnitee has not met such applicable standard of conduct, shall be a defense to the action or create a presumption that the Indemnitee has not met the applicable standard of conduct.

The termination of any Proceeding, or any claim, issue, or matter therein, by judgment, order, settlement (whether with or without court approval), conviction, or upon a plea of nolo contendere or its equivalent, shall not (except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement) of itself adversely affect the right of the Indemnitee to indemnification hereunder or create a presumption that the Indemnitee did not act in good faith and in a manner which the Indemnitee reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company, or, with respect to any criminal Proceeding, that the Indemnitee had reasonable cause to believe that the Indemnitee\'s conduct was unlawful.

For purposes of any determination of good faith under this Agreement, the Indemnitee shall be deemed to have acted in good faith to the extent the Indemnitee relied in good faith on (a) the records or books of account of the Company or any Enterprise, including financial statements, (b) information supplied to the Indemnitee by the officers of the Company or any Enterprise in the course of their duties, (c) the advice of legal counsel for the Company or any Enterprise, or (d) information or records given or reports made to the Company or any Enterprise by an independent certified public accountant, an appraiser, investment banker, or other expert selected with reasonable care by or on behalf of the Company or any Enterprise. The knowledge and/or actions, or failure to act, of any other director, officer, agent, or employee of the Company shall not be imputed to the Indemnitee for purposes of determining the right to indemnification under this Agreement.

**[Section 9. Remedies of Indemnitee / Enforcement]{.underline}**

**(a) Right to Bring Action.** In the event that the Company denies, in whole or in part, a request for indemnification or advancement of Expenses made by the Indemnitee pursuant to this Agreement, or if the Company fails to respond to such request within the time periods specified herein, the Indemnitee shall have the right to bring an action against the Company in any court of competent jurisdiction, including the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, to enforce the provisions of this Agreement and to recover the unpaid amount of the Indemnitee\'s claim for indemnification or advancement.

**(b) Defense.** It shall be a defense to any such enforcement action (other than an action brought to enforce a right to advancement of Expenses under Section 5 of this Agreement prior to a final disposition of the underlying Proceeding) that the Indemnitee has not met the applicable standard of conduct described in Section 2 or Section 3 of this Agreement, as applicable. The burden of proving such defense by clear and convincing evidence shall be on the Company. The Company shall not assert any other defense to any such enforcement action unless such defense is based on a provision of this Agreement that specifically limits the Company\'s obligation to indemnify or advance Expenses.

**(c) Expenses of Enforcement.** The Company shall, to the fullest extent not prohibited by law, indemnify the Indemnitee against all Expenses actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee in connection with any enforcement action brought by the Indemnitee pursuant to this Section 9, regardless of the outcome of such action, unless a court of competent jurisdiction determines that each of the material assertions made by the Indemnitee as a basis for such enforcement action were not made in good faith or were frivolous. No presumption of lack of good faith or frivolousness shall arise from an adverse outcome.

**(d) No Exhaustion Required.** The Indemnitee\'s right to bring an enforcement action under this Section 9 shall not be subject to the exhaustion of any other remedies, whether under this Agreement, the Company\'s Certificate of Incorporation, the Company\'s Bylaws, any insurance policy, or otherwise. The Indemnitee shall not be required to seek recovery from any insurer or other source before bringing an enforcement action against the Company under this Agreement.

**[Section 10. Contribution]{.underline}**

If the indemnification provided under Sections 2, 3, or 4 of this Agreement is unavailable to the Indemnitee for any reason whatsoever (other than as a result of the exclusions set forth in Section 7 of this Agreement), the Company, in lieu of indemnifying the Indemnitee, shall contribute to the Expenses, judgments, Fines, and Amounts Paid in Settlement actually and reasonably incurred by the Indemnitee in connection with any Proceeding in such proportion as is deemed fair and reasonable in light of all of the relevant circumstances, in order to reflect (i) the relative benefits received by the Company and the Indemnitee as a result of the event(s) and/or transaction(s) giving rise to such Proceeding, and (ii) the relative fault of the Company (and its other directors, officers, employees, and agents) and the Indemnitee in connection with the event(s) and/or transaction(s) that resulted in such Expenses, judgments, Fines, or Amounts Paid in Settlement.

The Indemnitee\'s obligation to contribute pursuant to this Section 10 shall in no event exceed an amount equal to the aggregate compensation actually received by the Indemnitee from the Company during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the Proceeding giving rise to the contribution obligation was first threatened, commenced, or initiated. For purposes of this Section 10, \"compensation\" means all cash and equity-based compensation received by the Indemnitee from the Company, including base salary, bonus, equity awards (valued at the time of grant), and any other remuneration for services rendered.

The Company and the Indemnitee agree that it would not be just and equitable if the amount of the required contribution were determined by pro rata allocation or by any other method of allocation that does not take into account the equitable considerations referred to in this Section 10. No person found liable for a fraudulent misrepresentation (within the meaning of Section 11(f) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended) shall be entitled to contribution from any person who was not found liable for such fraudulent misrepresentation.

**[Section 11. Insurance]{.underline}**

**(a) Maintenance Obligation.** The Company shall use its commercially reasonable efforts to obtain and maintain in effect, for so long as the Indemnitee may be subject to any possible Proceeding by reason of the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, one or more policies of directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O Insurance\") providing coverage to the Indemnitee that is at least as favorable as the coverage provided to the most favorably insured of the Company\'s directors and officers, on terms and conditions no less favorable to the Indemnitee, to the extent that such insurance is available on commercially reasonable terms. The Company shall provide the Indemnitee, upon the Indemnitee\'s written request, with a copy of all directors\' and officers\' liability insurance applications, binders, policies, declarations, endorsements, and other related materials in effect at any given time.

**(b) Notice to Insurer.** If, at the time of receipt of a notice of a Proceeding pursuant to the terms of this Agreement, the Company has D&O Insurance in effect, the Company shall give prompt notice of the commencement or threat of such Proceeding to the insurers in accordance with the procedures set forth in the relevant insurance policy or policies. The Company shall thereafter take all necessary or desirable action to cause such insurers to pay, on behalf of the Indemnitee, all amounts payable as a result of such Proceeding in accordance with the terms of such policy or policies. The Company shall not take any action, or fail to take any action, that would cause or permit the D&O Insurance carrier to deny, disclaim, or reduce coverage with respect to any claim made by or on behalf of the Indemnitee.

**(c) Survival.** The Company\'s obligations under this Section 11 shall survive termination of the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status for so long as the Indemnitee may be subject to any possible Proceeding by reason of the Indemnitee\'s former Corporate Status. In the event of any termination, cancellation, non-renewal, or material reduction in coverage of any D&O Insurance policy, the Company shall promptly notify the Indemnitee in writing. The Company shall use its commercially reasonable efforts to maintain or replace such coverage on terms and conditions that are no less favorable to the Indemnitee than the terms and conditions of the expiring or terminated policy, to the extent such coverage is available on commercially reasonable terms.

**[Section 12. No Limitation by Insurance]{.underline}**

The obligations of the Company under this Agreement shall not be reduced, limited, or impacted in any way by the existence or non-existence, or the scope, amount, or terms of, any D&O Insurance or any other insurance policy maintained by or on behalf of the Company. The Company\'s indemnification and advancement obligations hereunder are primary, and any right of the Indemnitee to receive payments or benefits under any insurance policy shall be secondary to the Indemnitee\'s rights to indemnification and advancement under this Agreement. The Company shall perform its obligations under this Agreement without regard to whether a D&O Insurance policy or any other insurance policy is in force, has been cancelled, has expired, has been exhausted, or otherwise fails to provide coverage for any Proceeding or any Expenses, judgments, Fines, or Amounts Paid in Settlement. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to limit the Company\'s obligation to indemnify the Indemnitee in the event that the Company\'s D&O Insurance policy is not renewed, is cancelled, is exhausted, or otherwise becomes unavailable to the Indemnitee.

**[Section 13. Subrogation]{.underline}**

In the event of any payment by the Company under this Agreement, the Company shall be subrogated to the extent of such payment to all of the rights of recovery of the Indemnitee against any insurer (including, without limitation, any directors\' and officers\' liability insurer), indemnitor, or other person or entity, and the Indemnitee shall execute all papers reasonably required and take all action reasonably necessary to secure such rights, including execution of such documents as are necessary to enable the Company to bring suit to enforce such rights. The Company\'s subrogation rights under this Section 13 shall be subject to, and limited by, the terms and conditions of any applicable insurance policy, including any subrogation or anti-subrogation provisions contained therein.

The Indemnitee shall not settle or otherwise compromise any claim that the Indemnitee may have against any insurer (including, without limitation, any D&O Insurance carrier) or any other person or entity from whom the Indemnitee is entitled to receive payment or reimbursement in connection with a Proceeding without the prior written consent of the Company, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The Indemnitee shall cooperate in good faith with the Company in connection with the Company\'s exercise of its subrogation rights under this Section 13.

**[Section 14. Non-Exclusivity of Rights]{.underline}**

The rights of the Indemnitee under this Agreement shall not be deemed exclusive of any other rights to which the Indemnitee may at any time be entitled under any provision of the DGCL, the Company\'s Certificate of Incorporation, the Company\'s Bylaws, any vote of stockholders or Disinterested Directors, any other agreement (whether or not the Company is a party thereto), any insurance policy, or otherwise, both as to action in the Indemnitee\'s official capacity and as to action in another capacity while holding such office or position. The indemnification and advancement of Expenses provided under this Agreement shall continue as to the Indemnitee even if the Indemnitee has ceased to serve in a Corporate Status, and shall inure to the benefit of the heirs, executors, and administrators of the Indemnitee. To the extent that a change in the DGCL or other applicable law, whether by statute or judicial decision, permits greater indemnification or advancement of Expenses than would be afforded currently under the Company\'s Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws, and this Agreement, it is the intent of the parties hereto that the Indemnitee shall enjoy by this Agreement the greater benefits so afforded by such change. No right or remedy herein conferred is intended to be exclusive of any other right or remedy, and every other right and remedy shall be cumulative and in addition to every other right and remedy given hereunder or now or hereafter existing at law or in equity or otherwise.

**[Section 15. Specific Performance]{.underline}**

The parties hereto acknowledge that the Indemnitee shall be entitled to specific performance of the Company\'s obligations under this Agreement, including, without limitation, the right to compel advancement of Expenses under Section 5 and payment of indemnification amounts under Sections 2, 3, and 4. The Company and the Indemnitee acknowledge that a breach by the Company of its obligations under this Agreement would cause irreparable harm to the Indemnitee, for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, the Indemnitee shall be entitled to seek and obtain injunctive relief, specific performance, and any other equitable remedies available under applicable law, in addition to any other remedies available at law. The Company hereby waives any requirement that the Indemnitee post a bond or other security in connection with any request for equitable relief under this Agreement.

**[Section 16. Severability]{.underline}**

If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable for any reason whatsoever: (a) the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Agreement (including, without limitation, each portion of any section of this Agreement containing any such provision held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that is not itself held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable) shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby; and (b) to the fullest extent possible, the provisions of this Agreement shall be construed so as to give effect to the intent manifested by the provision held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable. In the event that the indemnification or advancement of Expenses provided under any provision of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to exceed the maximum scope of indemnification or advancement permitted by applicable law, the Company shall nevertheless indemnify or advance Expenses to the Indemnitee to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law. The parties agree that any provision of this Agreement that is held to be overbroad shall be reformed, rather than invalidated, to the extent necessary to render it enforceable.

**[Section 17. Duration]{.underline}**

This Agreement shall continue in full force and effect regardless of whether the Indemnitee continues to serve as a director, officer, employee, or agent of the Company or of any other Enterprise at the request of the Company. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of, and shall be enforceable by, the parties hereto, including their respective successors (including any direct or indirect successor by purchase, merger, consolidation, or otherwise to all or substantially all of the business or assets of the Company), assigns, spouses, heirs, executors, administrators, and personal and legal representatives.

The Company shall require and cause any successor (whether direct or indirect, by purchase, merger, consolidation, or otherwise) to all, substantially all, or a substantial part of the business or assets of the Company, by written agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Indemnitee, expressly to assume and agree to perform this Agreement in the same manner and to the same extent that the Company would be required to perform if no such succession had taken place. The Company shall provide written evidence of such assumption to the Indemnitee within thirty (30) days following the closing of any such transaction. Failure of the Company to obtain such assumption and agreement prior to the effectiveness of any such succession shall be a breach of this Agreement and shall entitle the Indemnitee to the same rights and remedies as if the Company had denied the Indemnitee\'s request for indemnification.

This Agreement shall survive and apply to any Proceeding whenever arising from any event, occurrence, or circumstance that took place during the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, regardless of when such Proceeding is threatened, commenced, or completed. The Indemnitee\'s rights under this Agreement shall not expire, lapse, or otherwise be limited by reason of the passage of time, the termination of the Indemnitee\'s Corporate Status, or any other event, except as expressly set forth in this Agreement.

**[Section 18. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

**(a) Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to the principles of conflicts of law thereof that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. To the extent that the DGCL is applicable to the subject matter of this Agreement, the DGCL shall govern.

**(b) Forum Selection.** Any action or proceeding seeking to enforce any provision of, or based on any right arising out of, this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware does not have subject matter jurisdiction, another state court located in the State of Delaware, or if no state court located in the State of Delaware has subject matter jurisdiction, the United States District Court for the District of Delaware), and each of the parties hereto hereby irrevocably consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts in any such action or proceeding and irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any objection that it may now or hereafter have to the laying of the venue of any such action or proceeding in any such court, and any claim that any such action or proceeding brought in any such court has been brought in an inconvenient forum. Process in any such action or proceeding may be served on any party anywhere in the world, whether within or without the jurisdiction of any such court.

**(c) Entire Agreement.** This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings, oral, written, and implied, between the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof; *provided, however*, that this Agreement is a supplement to and in furtherance of the Company\'s Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws, and any resolutions adopted pursuant thereto, and shall not be deemed a substitute therefor, nor to diminish or abrogate any rights of the Indemnitee thereunder. In the event of a conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the terms of the Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws, or any resolution of the Board, the terms that provide the Indemnitee with the broadest indemnification and advancement rights shall control.

**(d) Amendments and Waivers.** No supplement, modification, or amendment of this Agreement shall be binding unless executed in writing by both of the parties hereto. No waiver of any of the provisions of this Agreement shall operate as a waiver of any other provision (whether or not similar), nor shall any waiver constitute a continuing waiver, unless otherwise expressly provided therein. No waiver shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement of the waiver is sought. No amendment, modification, or waiver of this Agreement shall be effective if such amendment, modification, or waiver would diminish or limit the rights of the Indemnitee under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Indemnitee.

**(e) Notices.** All notices and other communications required or permitted hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given when (i) delivered by hand (with written confirmation of receipt), (ii) sent by nationally recognized overnight courier service (with next business day delivery guaranteed and written confirmation of receipt), or (iii) sent by certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. **(f) Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall for all purposes be deemed to be an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same Agreement. Electronic signatures (including DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or other similar electronic signature services) and signatures delivered by facsimile or portable document format (PDF) transmission shall be treated as original signatures for all purposes of this Agreement.
